reranked_evidence.title: End of migrant protections creates elder care staffing challenges - PBS
reranked_evidence.snippet: Hundreds of thousands of migrants are facing uncertainty after the Supreme Court cleared the way for the Trump administration to end Temporary Protected Status for Syrian and Haitian nationals. It's raising alarm among leaders in the senior care industry, who say workers with TPS make up a significant part of a strained workforce. Hundreds of thousands of migrants in the U.S. are facing uncertainty, as protections that allow them to live and work here near expiration. That comes after the Supreme Court cleared the way last month for the Trump administration to end Temporary Protected Status, or TPS, for Syrian and Haitian nationals. Now, that looming loss of those protections is raising alarm among leaders in the senior care industry, who say workers with TPS make up a major part of an already strained work force. To what extent does the senior care industry, to include residential facilities and in-home care, rely on workers who are here under Temporary Protected Status?

reranked_evidence.title: Black members of Oklahoma Native American tribe file federal lawsuit to gain citizenship rights - Greenwich Time
reranked_evidence.snippet: Two descendants of Black people once enslaved by a Native American tribe are asking a federal court in Oklahoma to force tribal leaders to issue them citizenship cards as ordered a year ago by a tribal court. A lawsuit filed Thursday in U.S. District Court in Oklahoma City on behalf of Rhonda Grayson and Jeffrey Kennedy names Principal Chief David Hill and the Muscogee Nation Citizenship Board as defendants. It says that Hill and the citizenship board are violating an 1866 treaty between the tribe and the U.S. government by refusing to recognize Black Creek Freedmen as citizens as ordered by the Muscogee Nation Supreme Court in July 2025. The board had denied the applications of Grayson and Kennedy in 2019 because they could not identify a lineal descendant of the tribe, but the court said the pair are entitled to tribal citizenship.
